The heat flux expression for anisotropic media is generalized from the Polder-van Hove formula for isotropic media.
The hyperbolic bands in mHMM are formed by the coupling of surface phonon polaritons in the individual layers via the intermediate layers.
The group velocity in the direction parallel to the interface of the modes in the type I hyperbolic band can be negative, leading to negative or anomalous refraction.

For small distances (d < 100 nm), the HTC of an mHMM with SiC as the topmost layer is slightly larger than that of two SiC semi-infinite materials due to the extra contribution of the hyperbolic modes.
The HTC of a single 10 nm SiC layer on a Ge substrate interpolates between the HTC of the mHMM with SiC on top and the mHMM with Ge on top, depending on the distance.
Effective medium theory (EMT) overestimates the extent of the hyperbolic bands compared to the exact results, and it lacks the contribution from the surface modes.
The broadness of the hyperbolic bands in mHMM can be controlled by adjusting the filling fraction, with the largest bands obtained for a filling fraction of 0.5 in the case of a SiC/Ge mHMM.
